question.text: A metre scale is balanced on a knife edge at its centre. When two coins, each of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> are put one on the top of the other at the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> mark the scale is found to be balanced at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> mark. The mass of the metre scale is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
Let the mass of the scale be m.

The centre of mass of the scale will be at 50 cm.

Applying torque balance, 

0=mg×50-40-2×10g×40-10⇒m=60 g=6×10-2 kg
